timeline.event: Emperor Claudius launches the Roman conquest of Britain
timeline.label: 43 CE

timeline.event: Construction of Hadrian's Wall begins
timeline.label: 122 CE

timeline.event: Alfred the Great defeats the Vikings at the Battle of Edington
The Battle of Hastings is fought
The Domesday Book survey of England is compiled
King John seals Magna Carta at Runnymede
The Black Death reaches England
Henry Tudor wins the Battle of Bosworth Field
The Spanish Armada is defeated
Guy Fawkes and the Gunpowder Plot are foiled
The Great Fire of London destroys much of the City
The Acts of Union create the Kingdom of Great Britain
Parliament passes the Slavery Abolition Act
Women over thirty win the right to vote in general elections
The RAF fights the Battle of Britain
The National Health Service is founded
Elizabeth II is crowned at Westminster Abbey
The Channel Tunnel opens to France
London hosts the Summer Olympic Games for a third time

places.name: London
places.clue: Its Underground railway, opened in 1863, is the oldest metro system in the world.

places.name: Edinburgh
places.clue: Its castle crowns the plug of a long-extinct volcano, and a cannon is fired from it at one o'clock most days.

places.name: Stonehenge
places.clue: Some of its smaller 'bluestones' were hauled more than 200 km from the Preseli Hills of west Wales.

places.name: Giant's Causeway
places.clue: Around 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, mostly hexagonal, formed here as ancient lava cooled and cracked.

places.name: Loch Ness
places.clue: This deep Highland loch holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined.

places.name: Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa)
places.clue: A rack-and-pinion railway has hauled visitors up Wales's highest mountain since 1896.

places.name: York
places.clue: Founded by the Romans as Eboracum, it is where Constantine was proclaimed emperor in 306 CE.

places.name: Land's End
places.clue: Mainland England's westernmost tip is the traditional start of the 874-mile trek to John o' Groats.

places.name: Housesteads Roman Fort
places.clue: One of the best-preserved forts on Hadrian's Wall, which ran 73 miles from coast to coast.

places.name: Lindisfarne
places.clue: A Viking raid on this tidal island's monastery in 793 is often seen as the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

places.name: Iona
places.clue: St Columba founded a monastery on this small Hebridean island in 563, making it a cradle of Scottish Christianity.

places.name: Ironbridge Gorge
places.clue: The world's first major cast-iron bridge was raised across the River Severn here in 1779.
